Jayell Smoke House catered our wedding on 6/28/2019.  The wedding was just outside of the Lansing area.  The wife and I, and our guests, were more than pleased with the food.  Here was our menu:

Appetizer: Burnt Ends
3 Meats: Brisket, Pulled Pork, Mix of Spicy and Regular Sausage
Sides:  Cornbread Bake, Potato Salad and Baked Beans

We really liked how they pulled their smoker out to the wedding venue and cooked on the spot-it was a really nice touch for our barn-wedding and many of the guests commented about how they loved pulling up to the wedding and could see and smell dinner.  While we were eating my wife's brother had no shame in mentioning that the cornbread bake was in his 'top 5 things' he's ever eaten.  I completely agree!

We also felt that the value was quite reasonable.  Weddings are expensive, and to be honest our dinner was one of the few things that I really felt was priced competitively.  Working with the folks at Jayell's was really easy too-they were prompt with returning phone calls and when we went for initial tasting they were very low pressure.  The food was so good that it did that talking all on it's own.

One of my favorite things was that the gentleman that catered the wedding held back a few servings of the appetizers for the head table, since we were busy taking pictures when everyone else got to enjoy them.

I 100% plan to make the trek to Romeo for some carry-out in the near future and would easily let them cater any future event.

I topped my ketchup sandwich with another sauce (I didn't realize he'd be bringing me another) and was still fairly good and finished eating it (I hate to waste food if it's still edible), and got to take home the untouched sandwich. Iron Grate is a tucked-away spot in Cudahy boasting a real southern BBQ experience.

Food:  We split the 3 meat/3 side meal with a side of Burnt ends. Starting with the sides, the Mac and Cheese and cornbread were fine, but the standout was the baked beans. Highly recommend, as they see less barbecue like, and more like a thick, flavorful bean soup. Maybe less traditional, but very tasty.

When it comes to the meats, the hotlinks were a bit dry, and didn’t have the spice you might expect. The ribs were huge, but not your traditional cut. That said, it was almost like a meatier, tougher pork belly. Very tasty, but different. The brisket was on point, very soft and melts. All said, the all-star for my wife and I were the burnt ends. Melty bits of fat that paired perfectly with their sweeter hot sauce. Highly recommend.
Atmosphere: Odd, to be honest. The ordering line has a cafeteria vibe, however you get to see them prepare the food to order. The sitting area doesn’t seem to mesh with a barbeque joint, but the outside seating area would be perfect for the summer.

Service: Cashier was very helpful in ordering, and waiter we prompt and kind.

My score: 8/10. If I had to say one thing about Iron Grate, is it is a space that really does its own thing. Great barbeque, but may not touch to a true southerners roots the way that a down-home joint may. All said, the food was very good and would definitely recommend.

Fun new beer bar/restaurant in Elmhurst. High tech meets craft beer in a highly effective, efficient, and elegant way. In short, this place is a pour-your-own beer place where you pay per oz so you can sample many beers and even a few wines and pour whatever amount you want of each. They also have a full kitchen serving up some delicious barbecue. Tax and gratuity is included in all prices.

As you walk in, you'll be greeted and asked for your ID and a credit card. They'll keep your credit card up from like an open tab and give you a Pour Card. Once you're seated, you'll be able to order from a full barbecue menu. There are appetizers, salads, desserts, and plenty of great entrées to choose from, so don't only think of this place as a bar (though just drinking and not ordering food is also usual here). Ordering food is a very new (for 2017) experience where you'll use a little tablet fixed to the side of your table to put in your order exactly as you want it. While you wait for your food to come out, you might as well get to the main course and go samples some beers and pour a pint of your favorite. There is a  selection of 40+ craft beers, mostly local, from a variety of breweries and beer types. Two beer assistants were available and gave friendly input whenever we had questions or thoughts on the beers we were sampling. Across the 4-5 I sampled, I had some amazing beers and really nothing less than damn good. A waitress arrived with our food quickly, and we enjoyed what turned out to be a delicious entrée of brisket, mac n cheese, and sweet potato fries. Hanging casually is encouraged as there's no rush to leave, and we hung around and had a few more beers and more sampling. All in all, it was a great casual time and we'll definitely be back. Highly recommend.

• the sausage link was a surprising favorite at the table.  Heck, it's five bucks, throw one in your order
• the Bloody Mary - share with your significant other because it's too much for one
• the owners - they came to our table and visited and were super cool.  Your meat is in great hands with Greg and Kristina

Bottom line, if you like meat, you may have found your new best friends.

Just, it cannot be said enough, this place is spectacular! I wish I'd made it in sooner. Had the meat of the day, which was some sorts of burnt ends, soaked in their own juices, then instilled with some dark arts magic, causing me to completely forget how good the brisket was... Flavorful, tender, Smokey, Bold, but not pushy, like a lumberjack holding a kitten... I also had smoked Polish sausage, which was firm, juicy, with a good strong composition to it, salty and Smoky flavors, perfectly complimented by the light splashes of barbeque sauce drizzled over the sausage, and the brisket.  The bottle said Kentucky bourbon, and it certainly isn't wrong.  I definitely taste Kentucky bourbon, or at least the essence of, enriching a well smoked, not too sweet sauce.  I also had the foresight to grab a little cup of the spicy version, and it does not fail.  The spice is a slow buildup to a very light but steady burning sensation, neither getting hotter, or cooler as long as you're eating it.

Now then, there were some weak points ( minor as they are) that keep me from hacking Google's mainframes, and forcing a 7 star rating on this place.

The corn bread, didn't care for it.  It seemed a little mushy compared to what I normally expect from cornbread.

The smoked Mac n cheese, wasn't that Smokey, and compared to everything else on my plate, had a much more muted flavor profile to it, to the point it didn't taste like anything at all after I had the spicy sauce.  When I tried it again later, I discovered a more complex, albeit quiet subset of flavors. Unfortunately, it gets lost under everything else.

Kickin’ BBQ in the Butt

When I travel, I love interacting with people. They can steer you to the best places in their states, towns or cities. While at the Chazen Museum of Art, I spoke to a security guard about a place that serves good barbeque. I told him that I was from Kansas and we know “Q”. Immediately he suggested Bob’s Bitchin’ Barbeque. With a name like that, I had to check it out.
Located in a small downtown area, the 1905 building had been home to a couple of hardware stores and used as a billiard hall.
Bob’s serves their meat hickory wood smoked in-house dry and seasoned. It can be served “wet” allowing the sauce to caramelize over heat or “dry” to allow you to sample the eight different sauces that you’ll find at your table.
Under the dinner section of the menu I ordered the Sampler platter; 1/3 rack of ribs, pulled pork and a pork chop that’s brined and hickory smoked that gives a ham taste. I had a choice of two made from scratch sides; coleslaw and baked beans. It also comes with a side of corn bread.
The taste was incredible as the meat fell off the bones with every bite. I’m serious. Those ribs were so good I would slap someone if they tried to take my food away! My favorite sauces were as follows:
Original, which has a hickory smoked flavor.
RBQ, “Sweet with a little fizz with Sprecher’s Root Beer.”
Mango Red Pepper, “Sweet with heat.”
I enjoyed the coleslaw with a kick of sweetness and the cornbread was moist and tasty.
Bob’s bragging rights are that in 2015, his Carolina sauce won 1st place in the Mustard division of the American Royal World Series of Barbecue Sauce contest in Kansas City. In 2016, it brought home the bronze. And to think I had to travel to Dodgeville, WI to find all this out.
Overall: If this place was any closer, I would be a regular. In the meantime, I will make the trip again in the near future for those melt in your mouth ribs and sides.

Heaven’s Table BBQ is a new BBQ restaurant in the new food hall on the east side of Milwaukee.

Food: We got the 4 meat platter (Sausage, rib tips, brisket and beef shoulder.) Our sides were coleslaw and baked beans. Going down the row, the sausage was very good tasting, but like many sausages at BBQ joints, it was dry. The rib tips were really good, but almost had that idea of oxtail, in that you are chewing the bits off the bone/cartilage. Might have been better to just get the rips outright. The brisket was my wife’s fav, and was very well done and juicy. The beef shoulder was much like a pulled beef, and was very juicy and good.

The sauces were ok, as 1 was really good, and one was WAY too sweet and ketchup-like. The slaw was not my cup of tea, as it was vary vinegary and simple. The beans however were some of the best I’d had in a while. Cornbread was good as well.

Atmosphere: This is a difficult item to rate, as the business is in the food hall. The Hall itself is nice, and  good place to go if people have different tastes in food.

Service: Our attendant was very nice, and food came out very promptly. It is more cafeteria style, so no real service except going to order.

Overall: 8/10. I would put this on the same list as Iron Grate BBQ. I couldn’t tell you which was better or worse, but I’d say very comparable. If you like BBQ, I’d definitely give it a shot.

I stopped by the evening of 2/9/2016 for dinner. This was the 3rd time I've been there, and definitely won't be the last.

First, a little on overall impressions and atmosphere. They have the place decorated with some pretty fun decor. It's nothing like Ella's Deli (which I find to be quite frightening), but they have a soapbox car hung by the door, and other fun and interesting items covering the walls. As another reviewer commented, the age range of the crowd there is typically 35+. The waitress was younger (late teens/early 20's?) but I'm not sure why age enters into the equation anyway. Moving on...

It was a cold winter night, and I was pleasantly surprised with how warm the restaurant was. There were lots of good menu options. My top picks were the Beef Dinner, Cajun Catfish, or the nightly special, All-You-Can-Eat Ribs & Chicken Combo for $13.95. I ended up going with the special. I was a bit nervous to go with an 'All-You-Can-Eat' special, as sometimes they're better described as an 'All-You-*Care*-To-Eat' meals, but I'm happy to say that isn't the case.

The ribs were great, and the chicken was also great. Smoky flavor infused throughout both. Rib meat was tender and fell right off the bone. They had BBQ sauce bottles on the table, but the smoky and slightly sweet flavor of the ribs required no added sauce. Similarly, the chicken was moist and tender. The side items, which included cole slaw, baked beans, garlic bread, and fries (in the shape of potato wedges) were also great. The price is a bit high, but for the quantity of food received, there's no question about it being a good value.

Some other reviewers commented on the age range of the attendees, salad bar, or health considerations of dining at Fat Jack's. If these are concerns for you, get yourself to Cosi, Panera, McDonald's, or Starbuck's - wherever makes your conscience feel fuzzy. If you want a great meal, get yourself to Fat Jack's.

Decided to take a drive for some BBQ today. I typically try to stay within an hour of Columbus. So I had read a little about 2G's and made the drive out to Bellefontaine. Ordered the 4 rib special, it came with 2 sides. I ordered collard greens, mac n cheese and ordered additionally baked beans and cornbread. Also an iced tea. Bill came to 15 bucks. Pretty cheap for the amount of food. Now for the food. The ribs, because that is what it was all about. These ribs had a phenomenal bark on them. Most ribs our wet when you get them but these dry as can be and had such a great taste, inside they were super moist. The ribs are cooked with hickory and apple wood. You could definitely taste the smoky flavor. The bones just broke into pieces as I tore the meat off them. No utensils here, that's what your hands were made for. No sauce even needed. The greens had the slightest touch of vinegar that blended well with them. Mac n cheese was of the baked version with just a small bite from the cheese. Great consistency. Baked beans were okay but could have used a little kick to them. They were still okay, Cornbread had a sweet taste to it and was nice and moist. Put some butter and it melted perfectly. Talked with George the owner for just a minute, You could tell that he is married to the business. Some people are in it totally for the money and then there are those that it is there life. He has been doing it for 9 years now and has definitely perfected his craft. The restaurant has probably 12 tables in it. Plenty of room. The waitress was on it, she checked in a timely manner and had refills when needed. I will definitely be back. Great story on the back of the menu. Pretty inspiring.

Warren is very fortunate to have a carryout restaurant with this high quality bbq. If you love bbq and haven't tried it, you're missing out!

I visited Blackwood bbq with the family over the weekend. I loved the unique decor. From the strung lights to the menu written on butcher paper. Everything just worked. Even the bathrooms  were decorated simply but cool.
We ordered the sampler tray. This definitely could be shared amongst 3 people. Comfortably. 😉. Loosen your belt buckle because you are not going to be able to stop!! The tray came with the following: Pulled pork, pulled chicken, brisket, Alabama chicken, sausage, 2 cornbreads, 3 sides ( waffle fries, brussel sprouts, cole slaw) and white bread. WOW!!!   The Alabama chicken (in the center) was amazingly delicious!! Great flavor, tons of chicken. The cornbread was perfectly sweet, with kernels. I couldn’t pull away from the pulled pork!!  The waffle fries were great. Not your typical style. These were hot, seasoned perfectly and they had a great crunch! Charred Brussel sprouts: ummm delicious! Great crisp with just enough maple. (A must try!) the cole slaw came in a generous cup. Thinking back I should have grabbed some with every single one of my bites of pulled meat. My daughter got the pulled pork sandwich and son got the pulled chicken bbq tacos.  The pulled pork had burnt ends, as it should. So my daughter being a daughter ate around the crispy flavorful ends and just ate the pork and roll.   My son ate the tacos so fast he started digging into the tray.  I guess he liked them!!
I was happy to see adult beverages. Bbq and beer. Yum! Had to!

Never had them before and learned the vendor who makes them also makes them for local Mexican restaurants! Where have these been all my life?!

The food has authentic BBQ credibility, is delicious, and is reasonably priced. The staff are friendly and helpful as well.  Definitely recommend Smoked On High.

The pork was very good, being smoked but not really seasoned or marinated. It wasn't too fatty, but I did have to pull out a few small chewy gelatinous pieces. The spicy hot barbecue sauce was quite good, being slightly sweet and slightly spicy. The mac and cheese had a spicy tinge to it as well. It was very rich but very good. No watery cheese here. Overall, a very good visit and I'll be back when I'm the mood for barbecue in Cicero.

The three meat plate was enough for 2 at lunch time and came with some great sides. The beans weren't what I was expecting, but man were they good. The cornbread muffins were decent albeit a little dry. The coleslaw wasn't anything amazing but I enjoyed it and would order it again. The BBQ sauce is good depending on what you're used to. I used the it sparingly though as the meats spoke for themselves.

For meats we had the Milwaukee Ribs, Brisket, and Pulled Pork. The Ribs were interesting as the pork belly is left on making them about twice as tall as what you'd be expecting. This adds a ton of flavor, but naturally leaves the ribs very fatty. That isn't at all a bad thing but might not be for everyone. The pulled pork was smoked well and delivered great flavor.

Now I didn't like the brisket, I F'n loved it!!! I judge almost all BBQ places on their brisket and that's the main reason for the 5 stars. It is perfectly sliced, passes the pull test and packs an amazing amount of flavor into the bite. It is everything you could want out of a brisket and more. You can tell they know how to tend to the fire and get good clean smoke rolling.

TL:DR Go here as soon as humanly possible and let your eyes be bigger than your stomach because the food coma and meat sweats are well worth it. Your taste buds will thank you, your waistband won't.

I went for dinner. We grabbed some mac and cheese, pulled pork, and ribs to go. I wanted brisket, but they were out.

The mac was good. It wasn't amazing, but it was good and I'll definitely order it again. The ribs were okay. It wasn't tough, but it wasn't melt in your mouth. It didn't even really pull away from the bone that well. The flavor was good, and with the mac it was enough food for me (and I'm a 200lb guy who hadn't eaten all day). The pulled pork was awesome. Plenty of bark, great smoke flavor, good texture. It didn't really need sauce.

Speaking of sauce, we had Kansas City sauce and South Carolina (?) sauce. The Kansas City sauce had a good, subtle spice to it and the slightest bit of sweetness. It had a little more tomato present than I would have preferred, but it was all around a solid sauce. The Carolina Sauce (it could have been the NC, I dunno) was a great balance of mustard and vinegar flavors with a little BBQ spice mixed in. It had a nice tang to it that played really well with the BBQ spices. No sweetness to be found, no tomato flavor present, though it looked like it could have still been an ingredient (the other Carolina sauce seemed more like a straight vinegar, this was a little red and a little thicker). I enjoyed both sauces, but lean more towards the Carolina one.

As I said above, serving sizes were good. The mac was probably a 6-8oz serving, which was plenty. The ribs were four ribs with a good amount of meat, weighed out at a little more than half a pound. The pulled pork was about spot on for half a pound (they weigh it in front of you). My wife eight about 3/4 of both her mac and the pulled pork along with the slice of included white bread. I ate the ribs and all of the mac and bread, and felt satisfied. I finished off the remaining pork, and feel stuffed. The portions might be tricky if you don't overindulge, they will likely be too much for one serving, but not enough to split or save for a second meal. If you are willing to push yourself a little, and it didn't take much convincing, then you should have no problem finishing it all and being perfectly content.

Decided to take a drive for some BBQ today. I typically try to stay within an hour of Columbus. So I had read a little about 2G's and made the drive out to Bellefontaine. Ordered the 4 rib special, it came with 2 sides. I ordered collard greens, mac n cheese and ordered additionally baked beans and cornbread. Also an iced tea. Bill came to 15 bucks. Pretty cheap for the amount of food. Now for the food. The ribs, because that is what it was all about. These ribs had a phenomenal bark on them. Most ribs our wet when you get them but these dry as can be and had such a great taste, inside they were super moist. The ribs are cooked with hickory and apple wood. You could definitely taste the smoky flavor. The bones just broke into pieces as I tore the meat off them. No utensils here, that's what your hands were made for. No sauce even needed. The greens had the slightest touch of vinegar that blended well with them. Mac n cheese was of the baked version with just a small bite from the cheese. Great consistency. Baked beans were okay but could have used a little kick to them. They were still okay, Cornbread had a sweet taste to it and was nice and moist. Put some butter and it melted perfectly. Talked with George the owner for just a minute, You could tell that he is married to the business. Some people are in it totally for the money and then there are those that it is there life. He has been doing it for 9 years now and has definitely perfected his craft. The restaurant has probably 12 tables in it. Plenty of room. The waitress was on it, she checked in a timely manner and had refills when needed. I will definitely be back. Great story on the back of the menu. Pretty inspiring.

I am pretty new to Korean BBQ. So far, I have only had it at Star and once at Masijta. In both case we were a party of four that broadly bought the entire BBQ menu (or at least all the really fancy dishes on the menu). In case this makes a difference, we ate at Star late during a weekday evening (from about 8-10pm), and at Masijta during a Friday afternoon/early evening. Any reader should be aware, all I really care about is how good the food is-- price, atmosphere, service, etc. are all distant, secondary concerns for me, and right now, I'm focusing on finding the best Korean BBQ in around town (I like other Korean dishes as well, but I've found not nearly as much as the BBQ). The comparison between Star and Masijta BBQ isn't even a contest-- they aren't even playing in the same league. Star wins the battle of the BBQ hands down. The quality of the meat brought to the table was considerably better/better prepared at Star (Masijta's meats were all grisly and tough, Star's were all tender and succulent). Not only were the cuts of meat superior at Star, the presentation was far better. At Star, every bit of meat looked to have been carefully rolled/arranged on the platter in a artistic presentation, and each piece had obviously been given some TLC to ensure it was up to par. At Masijta, the meat came out in a massive gloppy pile (all the meats) with no care given to selection/preparation of the individual cuts or it's presentation. I only mention the presentation here because I think it speaks to how much/little care goes in to selecting the cuts of meat for the BBQ.

So, as far as Korean BBQ goes:
Star gets 5 of 5 stars! ;) Every bit of meat was delicious!
Masijta gets 2 of 5 stars. The quality of the meat wasn't even average-- it was below average. Of what was edible, it was tough and grisly. The pork cheek wasn't even edible.

A friend of mine brought me here and I must say I'm pretty happy he did. This place has an atmosphere that's a warm combo of homey and inviting. The staff was very nice and helpful with the menu. Not that the menu was confusing or anything but there seems to be so many good choices. It's also BYOB here which is great. The meal started with house smoked bbq chip which I must say are probably the beat potato chips I've had, the smoke wasn't overpowering but it added a subtle flavor that had us asking for more. Also the house pickles were refreshing and tart, good for between meats to cleanse the palate. I got the two meat option with sliced brisket and pulled pork, combined with coleslaw and truffle Mac and cheese plus a slice of Texas toast. The brisket had a nicely developed smoke ring, wasn't dry and had good flavor, the pork was similar. The truffle Mac and cheese was thick and creamy with cheese and the crust on top was a good textural addition. They have four sauces available to add to the meat but it didn't really need it, however the tropical chipotle I believe it was, was my favorite. Overall I'd have to say BBQ supply was a refreshing take on BBQ in Chicago, I'd definitely come back.

He has always been the guy you order with and the guy doing the portioning, normally that's a great thing.  He is a Michelin star chef and the food is every bit the quality you would expect. The place is super clean and clearly a professional establishment as always. I'm disappointed to see the owner set such a poor example. The rest of the staff were all properly masked. It's one thing to not be masked as you cook food that will be served at high temps, it's another to be breathing on food as it's served. I'll be waiting until we move beyond all this to return.

This place is a little gem in downtown Mishawaka.  It stands apart from the other offerings in the area although it fits perfectly in the old storefronts of downtown.  There is no need for this place to be anything but what it is,  the food does all the work.   The simplified aesthetic, bright, clean, classic.  The order at the counter and seat yourself service.  The blackboard notifying customers what has already sold out.  The bench seat running down one side of the small but well spaced dining area.  The galvanized platters that the most meals are plated on. Nothing more than the goodness of pure and unadulterated of Smoked Meat BBQ.  Everything was delicious, the portions generous.  The prices fair.  The homemade cucumber pickles, the sides like Mac n cheese and fries and cornbread; perfectly down home yummy.  The sauces to die for. The entire meal was obviously crafted by someone who loves what they do.  Someone who has mastered the art of bbq.  The sauces were surprising.  My vinegar based sauce which was clear and I sticky, had a tang and bite that made the perfectly smoked pulled pork taste like like it was born in the exotic parts of the south.  The horseradish white sauce that my guest had was also unique and complimented the brisket like a pair singing harmony.
As long as you are not a vegetarian or vegan you will not be sorry you checked out the Prized Pig.

It is an order and sit sort of place which is in line with the BBQ spirit. Our initial impression was a little unpleasant as the hipster ringing up was having a terrible time with my credit card. He finally said, "Have you been having problems with it?" My husband quickly answered, "No, we have been using it all day." He switched registers and just as my husband started to hand him his credit card, it went through. (I usually don't have problems, although most places have chip readers now). Then, he asked if we wanted to leave the tab open which was kind of weird since we weren't getting any alcoholic drinks. Also, he had this big ordeal about how he wanted our credit card first so it could be under a name, not a number, but then he handed us numbers.  My husband just got an irritable feeling from the whole drawn out exchange.

Our food came out so fast we were a little flustered. Now, the food, it was very good. The brisket was slightly dry for the moist cut I requested. However, it was very flavorful and not grisly. I still prefer Legacy's brisket, though. The baked beans, baby back ribs, berry cobbler, collard greens, pickled veggies, though, were superb. Homemade sauces were good and varied. Cobbler needs ice cream, not whipped cream, coming from a real Southerner! People often came around asking if we were okay.

The feeling overall was super hipster/trendy, not the typical down to earth BBQ. Sides are separate so it adds up. We weren't sure if they had draft but they had some nice local beers listed.

So Penny's please just work on the checkout experience and the moisture of the brisket. And get ice cream for the cobbler.

Accommodations are rustic, mom and pop-ish, down home atmosphere with a cozy fireplace, warning, you wait for a seat by it. After the staff, seating and atmosphere, i expected to be disappointed with the food, something had to fall. Not a chance. Half Rack dinner with potato salad and baked beans. Beans were okay, not much sprucing up there, but the potato salad, Y.U.M. No question my second favorite potato salad EVER. Only second to my mom's. Now the ribs. The half rack reminded me of Dino in the Flintstone's drooling over his brotasaurus leg. The mound of ribs was much more than expected for a half rack. Meaty, dark smokey crust, nice red ring underneath and meat that litterally falls off the bone and melts in your mouth. No teeth required. The light dressing of bbq sauce was just right to give the smokeyness of the bark a slight mellowing, neither being to strong or to weak by themselves but as a dynamic duo, there was a BAM, POW and a BOOM in my mouth... Honestly, an absolute delight to the most delicate or robust pallet. A very rare ballance of smoke and flavor that is hard to come by. Ribs here make the top five of my all time faves, and being from St. Louis, in the "Show Me State", they showed me why they come with such high acclaim. Only real disappointment I had during my trip was, well, the baked beans(- half a star), and they were out of Budweiser(- half a star)... Will be back next time I am in town... Save me at least a full rack this time!!!

We ordered the duo meal with brisket and pork. Sides were horseradish cole slaw, deviled potato salad,  and the white cheddar Mac and cheese.  I also wanted to try the sausage,  so we ordered a single Gandy Dog.  We tried the classic,  vinegar,  and mustard sauces.

Overall a decent meal.  The value was good for the amount of food we got.  But I felt like everything was just slightly off.  The brisket was super fatty, which I understand is a different style choice.  It was tasty and beautiful,  but got less so as it cooled off.  The pork was a little salty, but was tender and juicy,  which can be challenging for pulled pork. That sausage,  though... that was incredible.  Great snap from the casing. Great flavor.  The Gandy Dog dressing was okay,  but not necessary.  I'd eat a pound of this by itself. In my opinion,  all of the meats were better without any of the 3 sauces

The sides were all just okay.  I was looking forward to some sinus rattling cole slaw,  but it only delivered a little bit of that flavor.  I'd have enjoyed if they went harder with the horseradish.  The Mac and cheese was good,  but more clumpy than creamy.  The potato salad was good,  but again nothing special.

The biscuits and pickles were on point as well.  Overall a good meal,  but I'd probably just get bulk meats next time.

The  moisture trapped in the container turned what might have been good fries into a soggy pile of inedible starch. We made a mistake in not waiting to order the fries until we picked everything else up so they'd be fresh, but the chef and management failed us by not having a plan for sending a better quality product out the door. Surely they know fries deteriorate instantly in a sealed aluminum container. They should see a large order and either wait until the last minute to cook the fries, or wait and cook them while the order is assembled and the bill is settled. And they need packaging that does not trap moisture.

So I give 4 stars for absolutely wonderful BBQ meat and sides other than fries. I look forward to writing a five star review when the head chef implements a better plan for delivering great fries to customers who make large carry out orders.

She let us know about the drink and entree specials for the evening. Everything sounded good, but I had heard all about the brisket so there was no way I was leaving without trying the brisket.

There you have it, I ordered the brisket sandwich. It came on a nice brioche bun unsauced, side of well done hand-cut fries, and a small cole slaw portion. I really enjoyed the fact that I could taste the meat before deciding how much sauce I wanted to add. It was smoky, trim, slightly dry but nothing that a dip in the au ju or homemade bbq sauce couldn't fix. It was definitely worth the trip. My friend had the pizza and while he wasn't sharing, it smelled great. Two people at the table had the side of kale and we were all blown away by how scrumptious the veggie side was - almost justifiable to swap the fries for the greens.

By the time we left at 8:30 every table on the patio was filled. The overhead lights were on and I was full and satisfied. Thanks Big Bricks for proving my initial fears wrong.

I’m going to start off this review by saying I am a little biased towards Hickory River Smokehouse. I have been there four times and I really like it. I know there are the naysayers out there that say “Oh this place is better” or “This place is the best” and blah blah blah. I have had BBQ in KC and Memphis and Georgia and Texas. I am not trying to say this place is the best in the world but it is solid. They have a variety of really good BBQ and sides.

The Pulled Pork is great. It has won multiple State Fair titles. I also like the Beef Brisket and the Baby Back Ribs. You can’t go wrong with either the Hot or Mild Sauces. The undisputed Hickory River Smokehouse Champion is The Cue Shoe. This dish will knock you out into a food coma. I am a big guy and I struggle with this mountain of culinary love. The foundation is Texas Toast then a heap of Pulled Pork soaked in your choice of sauce. Next they top it with French Fries and smother it in a delicious white cheese sauce.

The sides are also good. I have had the Mashed Potatoes, Sweet Corn Bread and the Mac & Cheese. If I could give them one knock it would be the Baked Beans. I just don’t like them and think it is probably a matter of preference, but you may love them.

The only location I have been to is the Peoria spot. I think the interior is appropriate and have had nothing but good service there. From my experiences the staff has been great.

If you want delicious BBQ at reasonable prices and good service then I highly recommend The Hickory River Smokehouse and Oh Yeah you gotta try the Cue Shoe!

We enjoyed eating here for the first time yesterday. We'd gotten hungry for barbecue and were reading the reviews and had been a little worried about what they said.
The wait staff here is very attentive! I know someone had said the portions here were small- I'd gotten the ribs and chicken combo and while the half slab on the plate *was* smaller than some I have seen, the platter was priced accordingly, as it was the same for ribs plus chicken here than I would just get a half slab and no chicken elsewhere. And after eating the meal, I felt comfortably full. I did see one could add another half slab to any meal for 6.99 which would be the price of a rib/chicken combo elsewhere, so surely with the extra half slab the portions are not small at all. My husband got the half chicken plate and it was more than he could eat, so the chicken is plenty, and also inexpensive as well.
The sides are good- the braised cabbage is done in an authentic southern style, seasoned up with meat. I also got the sweet potato which is served with cinnamon spread and you can get brown sugar and more cinnamon if you like. My husband got the baked beans which he remarked were excellent and also the collards, which although mild in taste, were punched right up with a splash of hot sauce.
I think the most important thing here is the genuine flavor of smoke--which being an avid barbecuer myself I can assure you that it tastes right. There is another place in town that I suspect pours liquid smoke in their brine and that flavor just overwhelms their meat, especially the chicken. Here the smoke tastes like it comes from the smoker and nowhere else.
We know we will be back, as this place does meet our standards. Our waitress told us that on Sundays the chicken is all-you-can-eat. I am looking forward to that and if I manage to have some room after dinner I will sample some of the pie. My husband tried a chiffon type pumpkin pie and it was marvelous!

Chicago BBQ should always be taken with a grain of salt, it's not the best compared to other offerings in the country, but there are definitely places that stand above the others. We arrived at Lillie's Q for an early dinner on a Thursday night and we were promptly seated outside. To start, we ordered the fried pickles with a side of ranch while our dining companions ordered the boiled peanuts. The appetizers came out scary fast, like within a minute (no exaggeration), but they were obviously just made, which made them fresh and delicious. The pickles had a nice crunch to them, but I was overall not that impressed with them. The flavor profile was kind of bland. For dinner, my fiance and I split the pound of tri-tip with a side of beans and sweet potato fries. The server went over the sauce offerings, and the mayo based sauce went wonderfully with the sweet potato fries. We enjoyed trying all of the sauces from the Carolina to the Spicy sauces, all of which slightly changed the flavor profile of the meat. The sweet potato fries were perfectly crispy and the beans were flavorful, I'd highly recommend these sides. The service was prompt, friendly, and attentive, so no complaints on this front!

The good:
+ The burnt ends were fatty and moist. I'd get this on a return visit.
+ The sauces are tasty. Four different types cover mustard, Kansas City style, hot Texas, and Texas.
+ The cornbread was interesting. It was pretty creamy and it was a generous portion.

The fine:
The beans were good but unremarkable. The fries were a little too salty but hot and crispy. The mac and cheese was inoffensive. Not a particularly deep flavor nor did it have any bite (it was a bit mushy).

The not as good:
- This was the thinnest sliced brisket I've ever seen, and it was dried out. I'm really curious as to the reasoning behind this. I was actually really surprised they served such dried out product. I would hope that in most places, if it's that dried out, it wouldn't be served.
- There was a bit of plastic in my burnt ends. The manager came to see us and apologize, and they gave us a few bucks off of our order. I'm okay with how they dealt with it; I was hoping there'd be a bigger comp for chewing on plastic but I'm glad they didn't argue with us.
- Slow service. The waiter was great; really friendly and he gave great suggestions. But there were two servers for the entire second floor. It took longer than I would have liked to get his attention for the plastic and check. (I went on a Monday afternoon).

I felt like I was back in Germany, where a tiny Coke cost almost 5 marks and giant beer cost three. Maybe things have changed since then but I digress.

When I asked for a regular glass they said that they only served alcoholic drinks in those. I said a pint-size glass would be appropriate, but she wasn't allowed to give me a Dr. Pepper in a pint glass. So she brought me my drink refill in two of the tiny little jelly jars. I felt like a kid at a party when all of the regular glasses had run out.

I'm absolutely certain I'm not the only person who has asked for this. It's definitely a Butch masculine restaurant and I'm not the only person who came in at lunch time and wasn't drinking alcohol. I wouldn't have given my 11 year old boy a glass that small.

It's a stupid problem, but I think this is an example of where the customer isn't right, it's corporate that's right. Well hear me now Smokey Bones corporate, it's a stupid idea to serve soft drinks in tiny glasses next to plates of food so big that you can't finish them. Listen to your customer base and move your customers from the Kiddy table.

I get that you're going for the Southern Vibe with mason jars and handles on them, but I want to enjoy my drink without having to constantly ask for a refill. And if you're picturing an idyllic time with neighbors at a barbecue or sipping lemonade out of mason jars on a southern porch in the hot summer somewhere in Georgia, those were full size mason jars not the tiny jelly jars you guys have.

So save those tiny little glass jars for the kids cups and contact your restaurant supplier now. I might be the only one who is saying it but most of your customers are thinking it or feeling it unconsciously... It's different and not in a good way. You could spend 300 bucks and have all the glasses you would ever need. It's one thing to be unique and yummy and special, and another thing to be out of Step.

I understand inflation, but the price you pay for what you get has gotten unreasonable. My wife and I stopped in at Woodstock for a late dinner. We both ended up getting the two-meat dish with brisket and pork ribs. My wife had the mac and cheese, while I got the brussel sprouts. Cornbread also came with both of our meals.

The cornbread was very good, with a little bit of sweetness to it. The mac and cheese was overall good. It is served with "rib jam," which I'm not entirely sure what it is, but my wife liked it. I thought the brussel sprouts were interesting - they are served with a sort of hot sauce and are an unconventional side for bbq places, so I wanted to try them out. I enjoyed them, and they seem like a good option if you're trying to minimize carbs with your sides. The pickles were very good as well - thicker than standard pickles and with a good snap to them.

On to the meat. I was impressed by the ribs. My understanding is that a properly cooked pork rib should be tender, but should still require a little bit of tug to come apart from the bone. That's what these pork ribs do, and what pork ribs at a lot of other bbq places don't, so I thought that this set Woodstock apart. The overall flavor of the ribs was fine - good, but didn't blow me away.

The brisket I have some mixed feelings about. The brisket here is served sliced and unsauced, which is what I strongly prefer (sauce can always be added, but can't be taken off easily). The pieces we received appeared to be cut from the point of the brisket, which is also good. The brisket had good bark to it. However, I think that they need to make sure that the people cutting the brisket are doing so in a more traditional manner. First, the pieces we received were 1 large piece that was maybe 1 inch thick - probably twice as thick as is generally served. If they had cut it into 1/2 inch thick pieces, it would have been easier to eat. The more concerning thing to me was that it appeared as though it was sliced with the grain of the meat rather than against the grain of the meat. Slicing against the grain for brisket is important for maximizing tenderness and ease of eating. The flavor was ok, and could have been a little smokier. Brisket is a hard meat to do well, but I think there are a couple of easy things they can do to take things to the next level.

Overall, the food was good, and the portion sizes you get for the price represent very good value. I think there are some relatively easy opportunities to take this from a 4-star to a 5-star experience. I would happily come back and try some of their other dishes.

A friend was visiting from NYC, & I thought she'd be the perfect person for this first-time dinner adventure. We got there just after work on a Friday, & although their policy is only to seat full parties, the hostess was kind enough to seat us despite the fact that our third person was running a few minutes late. "We're filling up quickly," she told us, "so as long as he's nearby, let's go ahead & get you a table!" She led us to a table upstairs, next to a balcony that overlooks the entirety of the restaurant, with a great view of the urban industrial space.

First, I ordered a $9 French Toast Manhattan (Ezra Brooks bourbon, maple, hazelnut liqueur, & walnut bitters), & it was love at first sip, truly. Good start!

Everything at Mabel's is a la carte, so while the meat is served with pickle slices, Cleveland kraut, & a slice of white bread, it doesn't come with sides. There are lots to choose from, though none of them is mac & cheese, the side I most typically associate with BBQ. (A Mabel's bartender on Instagram chimed in to tell me, "He's trying To create 'Cleveland bbq' not BBQ you can get everywhere else. Since Cleveland has so much eastern European influence, he's using that in a lot of things at Mabel's. I don't think Mac and cheese really fits any of that." Well, OK.) I ordered the baked beans with chopped brisket & jalapeños (good, but I didn't eat much of them) & a side of spaetzle & spicy cabbage, which was the winner in my book (& stomach).

Mabel's standalone meat option are brisket, pork belly, turkey breast, kielbasa, & ribs (pork, lamb, or beef). I don't really do bones or fat, so I went with the brisket, served fatty or lean (guess which I chose - though I still had to cut off a ton of fat). The meat was dry & perfectly smoked, with both BBQ sauce & habanero sauce on the table to use at will. Yum!

The sauce at Mabel's is mustard-based, using the Cleveland-made brand Bertman's. I actually loathe mustard, & I'd never had BBQ sauce that wasn't sweet & thick, so Mabel's unique sauce was a bit of a shock to the system: thin, liquidy, & yellow, with a heavy vinegar taste. But I really enjoyed it - so much that I slathered my brisket in it & inhaled the whole damn thing. It was like no BBQ sauce I've ever tried.

Unfortunately, my sometimes-sensitive stomach didn't love it as much as my taste buds did, & I spent much of the next day battling severe stomach issues. I have some serious acid erosion issues, & eating acidic foods can throw me off for days - & boy, did Mabel's mess me up. I'm disappointed because, frankly, I hadn't expected to like Mabel's as much as I did - & I really did. If I went back, I'd have to take it reeeeeal easy on the sauce. For that reason alone, I wish they had a tomato-based option (though I'm sure that Instagram bartender would chide me for saying so!)

In short: Mabel's was tasty, but I probably won't head back of my own volition. If someone wanted to try it out, I'd join them, though, or maybe I'll just stop by for a happy hour treat of a French Toast Manhattan with a side of spaetzle... Regardless, I'm glad to see Mabel's up & running downtown. Hometown boy Michael Symon is one of the top chefs in the CLE, & I'm thrilled that his newest project is bringing something a little bit different to the table.

I really was hoping to give this place a good review. I've heard a lot about it, saw other reviews and was really excited to have a bbq joint in the neighborhood. Unfortunately, I can say yet again, I'm disappointed with another bbq joint in the area.

Now, that said, there were some good parts and I'll give the Pros first because there was some good aspect to it. But the three stars is a stretch for me to give and only one factor made me decide to give that.

The primary reason I provided three stars instead of two is this is the first place in the SE Wisconsin area that I've found knew how to properly cook a brisket. I'm a bit spoiled, I grew up in the south, spent a lot of time in Texas, and have had some of the best most mouth watering brisket available, it's by far my favorite type of BBQ, so when I see it available I have to try it. That said, they got it fairly tender, it was still a little tough but not bad, had a really nice smoke ring, and wasn't dried out. Overall I'd say it was cooked decently, and better than I've had anywhere else in the region.

The baked beans were alright, nothing to get hyped about but not bad.

The burger my wife had she said was good as well and had good fresh toppings on it.

And from a price point it wasn't bad, especially compared to how many bbq joints have a price point which usually comes with either them trying to price according to other joints despite lackluster quality or they really have a product worthy of a $15-20 plate.

They also have a cozy location, friendly staff and good bar selection, I stayed for a drink while I waited and the crowd was friendly too.

Now, that said, there were some glaring flaws that kept me from giving a better rating and as I said, if it wasn't for actually having a decently cooked brisket it would have been a 2-Star.

Starting with the brisket, while it's one thing to properly cook a brisket, its another to make it shine and make it delicious. Anyone can throw a steak on a grill or a piece of chicken in a pan and pull it off at the proper time and thats what it seems like happened here. There was no flavor in the meat itself. The rub was non-existent in flavor but I could tell there was something on it, and from a smoke perspective, I could see the ring so it did penetrate but there was no flavor to it, no taste of mequite or hickory or applewood or anything, almost as if they just stopped by a side of the road firewood stand and used some chopped down pine tree for the wood. In my opinion, a good brisket should shine on its own and a BBQ sauce should be a compliment to it. With this, it would've been pretty much bland and not inedible but unenjoyable without using a highly flavored sauce.

The burger my wife ordered she said was good but definitely tasted like just a prepackaged patty. It was clearly fresh meat and toppings but with a host of other burger joints in the area touting quality burgers it takes a good show to stand out and with Smoke Creek advertising itself as a bbq and burger place it's not shining with their burger and definitely not a place we'd go "Hey, lets go get a burger from Smoke Creek" when we could do just about the same running up to Meijer and getting some patties from the meat dept. It wasn't a fast food burger by any means, but it was definitely just something you'd get if you got asked to go out and didn't like BBQ and it was all there was else.

Lastly, the cornbread. I ordered an extra order of it cause I LOVE cornbread, I'll whip up a batch just on a whim and eat an entire tray of it. But this was bland, dry, and burnt on the bottom. They were cupcake muffins of cornbread, tasted prepackaged and a burnt bottom where the cupcake wrapped ripped off half the bottom.

Overall, if I get a super big craving for BBQ I might come by again just to appease that itch but I could eat BBQ 4-7 times a week, I was really hoping this would be the place I could go once a week but I'm thinking it's just gonna be one of those once every few months kinda places if that.

I have to update this review based on a better experience and absolutely amazing communication from the owner. I took my fiancé for lunch for mothers day weekend, honestly not expecting much from prior experience, but I said what the heck... The Brisket was Delicious! The fried potato salad was as good as I remembered.  The service was great. I decided to update my review and saw that the owner had asked me to call so I did. We had an excellent conversation about the pitfalls of the restaurant industry, how its impossible to please everyone all the time and finding great help. I really felt her pain as I have been in and out of this industry my whole life, from a dishwasher to a manager, server to a line cook. I still must stand by certain things I don't like, but I also understand being in a small town, you have to cater to your crowd. The food is not bad, and not at all overpriced. I told her Federal Law, Visa, and MasterCard all prohibit retailers from setting minimum purchase accounts (information readily available for review on credit cards dot com, and several other places on the Internet). She told me the guy working in the back had a law degree and she could get him to come to the counter to prove it. I didn't have time to argue with her.

I'm happy to give my money to retailers who don't attempt to extort more money from a regular customer because they can't handle the low fees the credit card companies charge for their use. I'm not usually a defender of huge companies line Visa, but those charges help keep the system running without interruption, and pay for the credit card machines and infrastructure used.

The food I've tried is good, but not good enough that I'm ok with being told I have to spend double than I planned to for lunch just so I can use my debit card. A retailer should care more about customer relationships than nickels and times. Plus half the time I go there they're closed due to catering. Oh well.

We enjoyed eating here for the first time yesterday. We'd gotten hungry for barbecue and were reading the reviews and had been a little worried about what they said.

And after eating the meal, I felt comfortably full. I did see one could add another half slab to any meal for 6.99 which would be the price of a rib/chicken combo elsewhere, so surely with the extra half slab the portions are not small at all. My husband got the half chicken plate and it was more than he could eat, so the chicken is plenty, and also inexpensive as well.
The sides are good- the braised cabbage is done in an authentic southern style, seasoned up with meat. I also got the sweet potato which is served with cinnamon spread and you can get brown sugar and more cinnamon if you like. My husband got the baked beans which he remarked were excellent and also the collards, which although mild in taste, were punched right up with a splash of hot sauce.
I think the most important thing here is the genuine flavor of smoke--which being an avid barbecuer myself I can assure you that it tastes right. There is another place in town that I suspect pours liquid smoke in their brine and that flavor just overwhelms their meat, especially the chicken. Here the smoke tastes like it comes from the smoker and nowhere else.
We know we will be back, as this place does meet our standards. Our waitress told us that on Sundays the chicken is all-you-can-eat. We sat at the table service side of the restaurant and let me tell you the service was excellent. Our waitresses were extremely friendly and prompt. You get four of the Wings, which are also delicious. I have to honestly say that the appetizers were actually better than our meal. Especially with their signature sauces which we sampled with our appetizers and let me tell you they are delicious. I tried every single one and loved every single one.

As for our meal, that was disappointing. I got the brisket which was extremely fatty but you can't really complain too much about that as brisket can tend to be fatty. I wish I would have gotten the pork butt, as I sampled that off of my boyfriend's plate and it was delicious. As for the sides that you get with your meal...wow that was so disappointing. The mac and cheese is right on the edge of overcooked and covered in a packaged cheese sauce with crushed-up Cheez-Its sprinkled on top. Had a myriad of different offerings that we opted for. Bone-in wings, brisket, pulled chicken, pulled brisket sandwich, baby back ribs. Sides of cornbread, baked beans, onion rings, mac and cheese, green beans, and the house salad, along with a cheese fries appetizer.

The good: Baked Beans, Mac and cheese, Cornbread, pulled chicken, ribs.

The bad: Brisket, pulled Brisket sandwich, soft drinks, house salad, cheese fries. Service.

Baked beans were good, pretty sweet, little kick with some smokiness. Mac and cheese is about what you'd expect for a homemade traditional style. Green beans were good, but very peppery, resulting in them being spicy.

The wings were juicy, with a nice crisp skin. Good deal, and solid price. Pulled chicken had good falvor and was moist. Ribs were good, very tender, with good flavor from the smoke and rub.

The briskets both fell flat. Granted, Brisket is the hardest meat to do right, and they also missed the mark here, unfortunately. They say a good brisket is the flagship item of a quality BBQ establishment, and I would have to agree. You could tell that the rendered fat had dried back over the meat, and the bark was leathery. Overall, over 50% was inedible because of this, it was like smoked jerky.

Onion rings were a smaller portion, but solid overall. The cheese fries, well, they never came, which is why service gets a whopping 0/5 in addition to the cornbread not coming with the meals and we had to ask for them. The TVs are mostly playing the same things, even the ones side by side, with little variety. Nice atmosphere, outside of that.

Overall 2/5, and it would likely be awhile to come back around due to the better options just 10 minutes up the road near the mall.

I wasn’t a fan of their hotlink; although the links were hot tasting, the link itself was too fatty with little fatty bubbles. The look of the fatty bubbles alone was a turn-off, but the rests were just a leathery chewy mess. Not a go-to in my book; on the other hand, the ribs we're plentiful and pretty tasty. What lacked in smoke flavor made up for in a meaty, tender smothered in a mild flavor of barbecue sauce. If you like mild sauce then you will enjoy their sauce, but I was more of an enthusiast for a mixture of mild/hot combination barbecue sauce which was provided on the hotlink sausage. The only type of fires they have are the seasoned fries which I am not a fan of either but with a little barbecue sauce and bread, it makes for a delectable fries sandwich. There has been much to do about how they cook their ribs, well let me just say this because when LEONS first opened it was much the same as all neighborhood barbecue rib joints. Then the cooking staff changed hands right before the old man retired or past away. The style of how the meat was cooked changed from ALL SMOKED to BOILED AND SOMEWHAT SMOKE COOKED, kind of like the way CARSON RIBS cooked their meat. You guys remember CARSON RIBS right??! It was the same place that was popular for years and was a go-to for many events I went to back in the day. Folks just loved them some CARSON for it tender and meaty falling off the bone flavor. It was always a decent place but never understood why they were so popular when the meat was never OPEN PITTED cooked. Anyway, this place was decent and like most places, one day the meat is cooked to perfection, and the next time it is depending on the cook is just okay. I will probably go back just for the ribs and sauce. Thanks!

My suspicion is that they take 3 ribs and then cut them such that all of the meat is on the outermost 2 bones, making it seem like each has a ton of meat. But this takes 3 ribs that you might be able to charge $20 for and converts them into 2 that you can sell for $40. I don’t have proof of it, but it’s what I think is happening.

The brisket is overall above average. It’s cooked and served appropriately, with good texture and moistness. I think the flavor could have been a little more smoky. I can’t recall the sides that we had.

Overall, my impression of the food here is average to slightly above average. However, the prices are high compared to other good local bbq places. Therefore, I’m not sure how much value is here, and I can’t give more than 3 stars.

We came here with really high expectations, I'll break down everything quickly.

Staff and service - First up the service was awesome. The cooks showed the grill, the hostess and wait staff were all amazing. This is why it's 3 stars instead of 2.

Atmosphere - really well done, solid and homey. It was a bit cold in there though.

We got a ton of food, so we're able to try a lot of the staples on the menu.

Cup of Chili - flavor of this was ok. It has huge chunks of meat in it. Honestly I thought I'd love that but it's excessive and the chili is better tasting than the meat chunks.  Meat is a bit tough, not tender as I'd expect.

PIÑA ASADA - skewers of meat and veggies. As expected, 3/5. Pineapple is the best part. I think there are some greens on there but they are burnt and not good.

Smoked wings - HUGE. I mean big. Meat is not so smokey, unfortunately. A bit rubbery almost. Not a huge fan, I like my wings crispy though.  The Dona sauce was really strange and not for me.

Stuffed peppers - these were ok but nothing special. Onions were a bit too crunchy I'd say, should be saluted first or longer.

Pulled pork - nothing to write home about.

Chopped BBQ - this is 4-5 star level. This saves the place, I recommend this big time.

Beef ribs - decent, big, still not super tender but much better than the pork.

Corn bread - to me it was dry and flavorless. Others did like it though. The butter is unsalted FYI.  The cheddar and jalepeno in it saved this one.

Black beans - better from the can
Kidney beans - these are fine, worth getting probably if you like beans.

Bread that comes w meat - good toasted garlic bread

Sauces - the BBQ on the table is the best option. The hot sauce is good too.

Anyway, the food was 2/5 to us. With the service and atmosphere, even if food was a 4 I'd probably get this place a 5. But the food doesn't cut it and I hate to say it but it needs reworked and new recipes tested.  Much luck then though and I hope it improves because I'd love to have a 5 star joint like this near campus!

Their Texas toast is great, but good Texas toast isn't very difficult to make and doesn't make up for the meh to bleh experience of everything else.  I also tried the banana pudding. To their credit, it had fresh banana chunks in it and came looking really cute. However it could've benefited from the addition of a couple vanilla wafers layered within, but that would require being made-to-order to keep the wafers from going soggy. But it would help break-up and balance the banana flavor.  Not sure if the pudding was made from scratch.  It had that artificial banana flavor that I find all banana pudding has, so it might just be what homemade banana pudding tastes like. But the whip cream on top of it was pleasantly thick and just the right level of sweet.

Would I choose to eat there again? No.  Would I refuse to go if someone else wanted to? No, I just would know to expect a very non-exceptional meal.

Everything came out quick, the boys loved their food, but only ate about half understandably. I chowed my wings that were really good. Good smoke meat doesn't need sauce. Feel free to add if you like but it should stand on its own. The rids, chicken, and pulled pork came covered in sauce. It masked the smoke smell and flavor way too much. I should have asked for it on the side, but adding sauce shouldn't be the normal approach to smoked meat. Leave it alone and let the customer add it as they want. The sides were great all the way around. My wife loved her salad and craft beer. Kudos there.

I guess at the end of the night three things really hurt the experience - waiting and then having to find someone to help us who never apologized.
